claims.claim: The first transistor was invented in 1947.
claims.episode_span: The convention had been set by decades of vacuum-tube practice and simply carried over when transistors appeared in 1947.
claims.source_title: Invention of the integrated circuit - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: The invention of the first transistor in 1947 led to the expectation of a new technological revolution.

claims.claim: Jack Kilby of Texas Instruments patented the principle of integration and created the first prototype integrated circuits.
claims.episode_span: Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments and Robert Noyce at Fairchild independently asked what the raw physical requirement actually was
claims.source_title: Invention of the integrated circuit - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: Jack Kilby of Texas Instruments patented the principle of integration, created the first prototype ICs and commercialized them.

claims.claim: Robert Noyce of Fairchild Semiconductor invented the first monolithic IC, connecting components with aluminium metallization and using insulation based on Jean Hoerni's planar process.
claims.episode_span: Second, aluminum or later copper interconnects were deposited and patterned in the same sequence, eliminating the need for external wires between devices on the same die.
claims.source_title: Invention of the integrated circuit - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: He invented a way to connect the IC components (aluminium metallization) and proposed an improved version of insulation based on the planar process technology developed by Jean Hoerni

claims.claim: Modern consumer microprocessors contain on the order of tens to hundreds of billions of transistors; the highest consumer count as of March 2025 was 184 billion (Apple M3 Ultra).
claims.episode_span: A modern microprocessor die contains on the order of tens of billions of transistors yet sells for a few hundred dollars
claims.supporting_quote: The highest transistor count in a consumer microprocessor as of March 2025

claims.claim: Upgraded metallurgical-grade silicon cost about $1.70-3.20 per kg (2005-2008), roughly 10 times cheaper than electronic polysilicon, consistent with metallurgical silicon selling for a few dollars per kilogram.
claims.episode_span: metallurgical-grade silicon sells for a few dollars per kilogram
claims.supporting_quote: It is about 99% pure which is three or more orders of magnitude less pure and about 10 times less expensive than polysilicon ($1.70 to $3.20 per kg from 2005 to 2008 compared to $40 to $400 per kg for polysilicon)

claims.claim: IC prices collapsed during the 1960s: over the course of the Apollo/military computer programs the price for an integrated circuit dropped from about US$1,000 to US$20-30.
claims.episode_span: By the mid-1960s commercial integrated circuits were already undercutting discrete assemblies on price for equivalent function, and the gap widened rapidly.
claims.source_title: Invention of the integrated circuit - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: and during their manufacture, the price for an IC dropped from US$1,000 to US$20–30. In this way, NASA and the Pentagon prepared the ground for the non-military IC market.
